svg.title: Where Each Account Dollar Goes
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-account-cost-split; chapter number: 4; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Where Each Account Dollar Goes; subtitle: Labor-hour pricing with a 40/30/30 split and supplies billed on top; total range: 100% of base billing (40/30/30), plus a 3-5% supply charge; caption: Rudy Perez aims every account at 40% labor, 30% other expenses and 30% profit; Carolyn Arellano bills 3% of the base rate for supplies on top of the labor figure.; assumptions note: The 40/30/30 split is a per-account target, not an industry average. The supply band spans Carolyn Arellano's 3% and the 3-5% range cited across bidders.; note: Sources 7 Figure Cleaning with Rudy Perez (1_z-Kgj0GYM at 00:01:17); Carolyn Arellano (IJlyq2UAXqU at 00:06:05); AJ SIMMONS (7VHAkhs_HG4 at 00:02:48).; buckets: label: Labor; low: 40; high: 40; notes: AJ Simmons bills double the cleaner wage, $15 paid becoming $30 billed.; label: Supplies, insurance, taxes, CPA; low: 30; high: 30; notes: Load back office, transportation, churn and overtime before the account goes out.; label: Profit; low: 30; high: 30; notes: Rudy Perez's worked example uses a $40 hourly charge.; label: Supply charge on top of base; low: 3; high: 5; notes: 3% of a $2,166.66 base is $64.98 a month (Carolyn Arellano).
